title: Heritage sites in Uttar Pradesh: Taj Mahal, Sarnath and Varanasi
seo_title: Heritage Sites in Uttar Pradesh: Taj, Sarnath and 4 UNESCO
meta_description: Heritage sites in Uttar Pradesh: the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri and Sarnath (UNESCO 2026), plus Varanasi, Lucknow, Mathura, Kaushambi and Kushinagar.
keywords: taj mahal agra fort fatehpur sikri
summary: Uttar Pradesh has four UNESCO World Heritage Sites: the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri and the Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath, inscribed in July 2026. It also holds Varanasi's ghats, the Nawabi monuments of Lucknow, the sculpture of Mathura, the ancient cities of Kaushambi and Shravasti, Kushinagar, and the Gupta temple at Deogarh.

sections.h2: Why Uttar Pradesh is central to Indian history
paras: The Ganga and Yamuna plains of Uttar Pradesh have been settled and farmed for thousands of years, and the state covers several of the sixteen mahajanapadas, including Kashi, Kosala and Vatsa. The Buddha gave his first sermon at Sarnath and died at Kushinagar. Mathura was a great centre of Kushan sculpture, and the Gupta temple at Deogarh is one of the earliest stone temples in north India.

Later, Agra was the Mughal capital under Akbar, Jahangir and Shah Jahan, and Lucknow became the seat of the Nawabs of Awadh in the 18th century. The 1857 uprising left its mark at Lucknow, Kanpur and Meerut. Our explainers on [major dynasties of ancient India](major-dynasties-of-ancient-india.html) and the [Mughal empire](mughal-empire.html) give the background.

sections.h2: The four UNESCO World Heritage Sites
paras: Agra Fort and the Taj Mahal were among India's first World Heritage Sites, inscribed in 1983. The red sandstone fort was rebuilt by Akbar from 1565, with later marble palaces by Shah Jahan. The Taj Mahal, built by Shah Jahan as a tomb for Mumtaz Mahal from about 1632, is the most famous Mughal building. Fatehpur Sikri (1986), Akbar's short-lived capital of the 1570s and 1580s, keeps its palaces, Jama Masjid and the Buland Darwaza almost complete.

The Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath was inscribed in July 2026 at the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee in Busan, making it India's 45th World Heritage Site. It includes the Dhamekh stupa, the remains of monasteries and the stump of the Ashokan pillar, whose lion capital is now the national emblem and is shown in the site museum. See our [Agra heritage walk guide](heritage-walk-in-agra.html) and the programme [Fatehpur Sikri: Mughal urban vision](fatehpur-sikri-mughal-urban-vision.html).

sections.h2: Varanasi, Sarnath and the Buddhist circuit
paras: Varanasi's ghats, lanes and temples make it one of the oldest continuously lived-in cities in the world, with excavations at Rajghat showing occupation from about the early 1st millennium BCE. Our [Varanasi heritage walk guide](heritage-walk-in-varanasi.html) describes routes along the river.

Beyond Sarnath, the Buddhist sites of Uttar Pradesh include Shravasti, where the Buddha spent many rainy seasons at the Jetavana monastery, Kushinagar with its Mahaparinirvana temple and Ramabhar stupa, Kaushambi with its ramparts and Ghoshitarama monastery, and Sankisa. Our [Pali course](pali-a-first-course.html) is a good way to read the texts that name these places.

The Dashavatara temple at Deogarh in Lalitpur district, of about the 6th century, is one of the earliest surviving stone temples in north India, with famous panels of Vishnu on the serpent Shesha. Bhitargaon near Kanpur has a Gupta-period brick temple. Mathura's Government Museum holds the great collection of Kushan and Gupta sculpture made in the local red sandstone.

Later temples include those of Vrindavan, such as the 16th century Govinddev temple built under Raja Man Singh. Our lecture on [early structural temples](early-structural-temples.html) covers Deogarh and Bhitargaon in detail.

Lucknow's Bara Imambara, built in 1784 with its vaulted hall and bhulbhulaiya, the Rumi Darwaza and the Chhota Imambara show Nawabi architecture at its height. The ruined Residency recalls the siege of 1857. Prayagraj (Allahabad) has an Ashokan pillar inside Akbar's fort, Khusrau Bagh and the Anand Bhawan museum. Jhansi fort is linked with Rani Lakshmibai.

Our city guides cover walks in [Lucknow](heritage-walk-in-lucknow.html) and [Prayagraj](heritage-walk-in-prayagraj.html), and the tour [Three capitals: Delhi, Agra and Jaipur](three-capitals-delhi-agra-and-jaipur.html) adds Agra to a north India itinerary.

faq.q: How many UNESCO World Heritage Sites are in Uttar Pradesh?
faq.a: Four: Agra Fort and the Taj Mahal (both 1983), Fatehpur Sikri (1986) and the Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath, inscribed in July 2026 at the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee in Busan.

faq.q: When did Sarnath become a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
faq.a: Sarnath was inscribed in July 2026 as the Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath, India's 45th World Heritage Site. The listing covers the Dhamekh stupa, monastic remains and the Ashokan pillar at the place where the Buddha gave his first sermon.

faq.q: Which are the oldest temples in Uttar Pradesh?
faq.a: The Dashavatara temple at Deogarh, of about the 6th century, and the brick temple at Bhitargaon near Kanpur, of the Gupta period, are among the oldest surviving temples in north India.

faq.q: What are the main Buddhist sites in Uttar Pradesh?
faq.a: Sarnath, where the Buddha first taught, Kushinagar, where he died, Shravasti, with the Jetavana monastery, Kaushambi and Sankisa. With Bodh Gaya in Bihar they form the core of the Buddhist pilgrimage circuit.
